title: Smart routing fallback — incident breadcrumbs (scratchpad)
body:
High-level: scratchpad of commands, logs and hypotheses from morning of 2026-03-02. Incident: automated smart-routing fallback triggered for US-west->EU-west regional failover; some clients saw increased p95 latency and a small percentage of 503s when fallback path activated. Trying to capture breadcrumbs for postmortem draft.

Timeline / breadcrumbs (UTC):
- 2026-03-02 08:45:12 — Alert: routing-fallback-triggered (alerts via PagerDuty). Metric: route_fallback.count spiked from 0 -> 67 in 1m for model:gptx-small region:us-west.
- 2026-03-02 08:45:20 — Slack: #prod-alerts (thread id message-1642). Noted higher p95 (~2.6s -> 6.1s) for requests routed to fallback variant (model alt-quant).
- 2026-03-02 08:46:01 — Canary checks failed for new kernel selection in us-west edge pool, health-checks flapping; autoscaler did not add capacity quickly enough.
- 2026-03-02 08:47:30 — Temporary manual override: route-policy set to prefer region:eu-west for traffic-weight 20% (rollback @09:10).

Commands run (local runner + cluster ops):
- curl to check health endpoint (from ops laptop):
  curl -sS -D - https://us-west-serving-1.redwood.internal/health | tail -n +1
  -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  body: {\"status\":\"degraded\", \"uptime\":\"43h\", \"active_kernels\":87} (note: health shows degraded but 200)

- kubectl to fetch pod logs for serving runtime (us-west pool):
  kubectl -n serving logs deploy/serve-usw-1 -c runtime --since=15m | grep -i fallback | tail -n 50
  -> [08:44:58] WARN routing.go:254 fallback: triggered fallback for model=gptx-small reason=kernel-select-timeout
  -> [08:45:10] ERROR kvcache.go:112 cache-miss-rate=0.42 region=us-west action=evict-scan slow-evict=true
  -> [08:45:12] WARN routing.go:198 fallback-count=67 circuit-open=true threshold=50

- curl to API that exercises smart-routing header (simulate client):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Region-Preference: us-west' -d '{"model": "gptx-small", "prompt": "test"}' -i
  -> 503 Service Unavailable (x-request-id: zyx-23094) OR slow response ~5.8s with header X-Fallback-Used: true

- ran a quick traceroute to eu-west from an edge node to confirm latency curve:
  traceroute eu-west-serving-1.redwood.internal
  -> avg latency ~ 110ms (expected ~90ms) — small increase but not catastrophic

Logs / error snippets captured (raw):
- routing.go WARN: fallback: triggered fallback for model=gptx-small reason=kernel-select-timeout (08:44:58)
- kvcache.go ERROR: cache-miss-rate=0.42 action=evict-scan slow-evict=true (08:45:10)
- dispatcher.go ERROR: failed to allocate execution slot: err=allocation-timeout retries=3 (08:45:11)
- http responses: 503 \"fallback route unavailable\" (retries exhausted) (08:45:12-08:46:00)

Metrics snapshots (from datadog short window 08:44-08:48):
- route_fallback.count (us-west): 0 -> 67
- runtime_alloc.failures (us-west): 2 -> 15
- kv_cache.miss_rate (us-west): 0.08 -> 0.42
- p95_latency (us-west, model=gptx-small): 2.6s -> 6.1s
- traffic_shift.to_euwest: +12% during 08:45-09:00 window after policy shift

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selection timeout cascade: a recent kernel selector change (PR #981) changed fallback timeout from 150ms -> 75ms. This caused more frequent fallback triggers when kernel lookup is slightly slower under load, increasing fallback load on alternate variants and causing allocation contention.
2) KV cache thrash / eviction: sudden increase in cache-miss-rate (0.08 -> 0.42) suggests warm prefix cache got invalidated or eviction policy misfired. Fallback routing increases cold-starts for KV cache and amplifies miss rate, raising latency.
3) Autoscaler sluggishness for dedicated pool in us-west: configured min-replicas and step scaling may be too conservative vs sudden fallback surge. Long allocation-timeout errors in dispatcher.go support this.
4) Network spike to eu-west (slower RTT) amplified combined effect when fallback routed traffic cross-region; but traceroute shows only modest increase, so not primary.

Notes on recent changes to investigate:
- PR #981 (runtime): kernel selector refactor merged 2026-02-28 (owner @marcus). Claim: reduces time to choose kernel in common path, but introduced tighter timeout for fallback detection.
- Autoscaler policy changed 2026-02-20 for us-west pool (lower growth rate to reduce costs).
- KV cache eviction tweak landed 2026-02-25 (PR #967) that changed eviction heuristics for quantized weights.

Immediate next steps (what I ran / will run):
- Reproduce locally with load script: run locust scenario hitting smart-routing header to force us-west pref and observe fallback threshold. (cmd: ./tools/loadtest --region us-west --model gptx-small --qps 120) — started at 09:22, captured similar fallback triggers at ~85 qps.
- Temporarily increase kernel selector timeout on a small canary in us-west to previous value (150ms) and observe if fallback_count drops. (config override: runtime.kernel_selector.timeout_ms=150) — rolled to canary at 09:41, fallback_count for canary dropped to 2 in 10m.
- Rollback autoscaler step limits for us-west to allow faster scale-up (manual policy bump).
- Rehydrate KV cache: run warmup job to prefetch popular prefixes for gptx-small on us-west serving nodes (script: scripts/warm_kv_cache.sh --model gptx-small --top-keys 5000).
- Open follow-up Jira: INC-2026 assigned to @marcus and @olivia to run full postmortem, tag eng-serving-runtime and eng-sre.

Unresolved / TODOs:
- Confirm whether PR #981 intentionally changed timeout (talk to author Marcus). I left a comment on the PR but need explicit decision.
- Need to quantify how much of the p95 spike is due to cache misses vs allocation contention. Action: add temporary tracing for kvcache.hit vs dispatcher.wait_time on fallback path.
- Run a controlled chaos test to simulate fallback load and measure autoscaler reaction time.
- Decide on permanent mitigation: either increase timeout, add jitter to kernel selection, or make fallback route adaptive to current cache miss rate.

Scratch notes / things I told PD and SRE during calls:
- \"Primary suspect = kernel-selector timeout tweak (PR 981).  Reverting for canary reduced fallbacks immediately.\"
- \"KV cache miss spike probably secondary amplifier — warmup helps.\"
- \"Short-term: increase kernel-selector timeout back to 150ms on us-west pool and bump autoscaler step size. Medium: add guarding so fallback doesn't route >X% of traffic to alternative variants if region already under stress.\"

Links / refs (quick):
- PR #981: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026
- Slack thread: #prod-alerts (message-1642)

Notes to self for postmortem write-up:
- Include timeline above, key metrics, reproducer steps (loadtest command), and mitigation applied (kernel timeout canary, autoscaler bump, KV warmup).
- Add proposed long-term mitigation items and owners: Marcus (kernel selector), Olivia (autoscaler policy), Ethan (kv cache heuristics).

Random scratch (incomplete):
- Consider adding a circuit-breaker on route_fallback so that if fallback_count > 50 and runtime_alloc.failures > 10 we temporarily reduce routing weight to fallback variants by 50% and signal SRE.  Need to discuss viability w/ @olivia.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and push to postmortem doc after confirm with collaborators.
